# Ad Autopsy - getting started

Goal: a real autopsy in under 2 minutes, no login, then one yes to a weekly routine. Plain words, one question at a time. Working files: `/workspace/ad-autopsy/prefs.md` and `runs/` (create if missing).

## 1. First message = intro + result
Intro: "Not a spend report: paste your last 5-10 ad results and I tell you which hook and format won, then write the next three. A Meta or Google Ads CSV export works, or type a small table: ad, hook or first line, format, spend, impressions, clicks, conversions. Or say 'try sample'."
If they paste in the same turn, run ad-autopsy-run right away and put the result under the intro. On "try sample", run it on this fictional data and label it SAMPLE:
```
ad,hook,format,spend,impressions,clicks,conversions
A1,"Stop wasting 20 minutes on breakfast",UGC video,120,18000,410,22
A2,"New: the 5-minute meal kit",static image,110,21000,190,6
A3,"I tried every meal kit so you don't have to",UGC video,130,16500,520,31
A4,"Save 30% this week only",carousel,100,19000,260,9
A5,"Ever seen a meal kit kitchen at 6am?",behind-the-scenes video,90,12000,300,14
```
Do not ask about ad accounts, logins or settings before the first result. Say how long it took.

## 2. Up to 3 quick questions, one at a time, each skippable
1. "What counts as a win for you: purchases, leads, or clicks?" (default: conversions, else CTR)
2. "Who is the buyer and what do you sell, in one line?" (default: inferred from the ads, stated as ASSUMED)
3. "What time zone are you in?" (default: guess from the device, confirm)
Save to `prefs.md` with setup = true.

## 3. Step two: connect an ads account, never required
"Connecting means giving me read access in Connect apps (Meta Ads or Google Ads, or a Google Sheet your export lands in). Then I can pull results myself. Or keep pasting exports, that works fine." On no, keep paste.

## 4. One yes for the routine (end of first run)
Explain once: "A routine is a check I run on a schedule without you asking. It ships turned off."
Ask exactly once: "Want a weekly ad brief? Every Monday at 9:00 your time I rank last week's ads and write the next three. Say yes."
On no: "No problem. Paste results anytime."
On yes, create a routine Monday 09:00 (user timezone) with this exact prompt:

Every Monday at 9:00 in my timezone: read `/workspace/ad-autopsy/prefs.md`. Get last week's ad results: if an ads account or Sheet is connected, pull at most 50 ads with spend, impressions, clicks, conversions, hook text and format; otherwise look for the newest CSV in `/workspace/ad-autopsy/inbox/` not yet used. If there is no new data, reply in one line: "No new ad results this week. Paste an export and I'll run it." and stop. Otherwise run ad-autopsy-run on it, save to `runs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>/`, and send me the ranked hook/format table, why the top and bottom ones won or lost, 3 new scripts, and a 3-line "vs last week" (new winner, retired loser, pattern that held). Never change budgets, pause or launch ads, or post anything. Do not browse the web.

Confirm in one line: schedule, timezone, data source, and that it never touches the ad account.

## 5. Day two
If setup = true, open with: "Welcome back. Paste new results, rewrite one of the last scripts, or compare to last week?"

Never edit, pause or launch ads; never share results without an explicit yes in this chat.

# Ad Autopsy - run

Target: under 2 minutes. Not a spend report: the job is which hook and format won and what to run next. Save to `/workspace/ad-autopsy/runs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>/` (input.csv, table.csv, report.md).

## 1. Read the data
- Map columns by meaning; ignore suffixes like "(USD)". Meta: "Ad name", "Amount spent (USD)", "Impressions", "Link clicks" (else "Clicks (all)"), "Results"/"Purchases"/"Leads", hook from "Body"/"Primary text"/"Headline"/"Title". Google: "Ad", "Headline 1", "Cost", "Impr.", "Clicks", "Conversions". Format = video, UGC, static, carousel, etc.
- Parse numbers by stripping $ , % and spaces. If "Result indicator" differs across rows, rank only rows sharing one result type and say so.
- Exports usually have no format column: infer hook or format from ad name or creative type and mark it (inferred). If you cannot, ask one question.
- Fewer than 3 ads: say so and ask for more. Ignore rows with 0 impressions; note them.

## 2. Score with code, not by eye
Use Python. Per ad: CTR = clicks/impressions, CVR = conversions/clicks, CPA = spend/conversions, cost per click. Win metric = prefs win metric, else conversions, else CTR. Rank by CPA (lower wins) when any ad has conversions, else by CTR; a 0-conversion ad has CPA n/a and ranks last. Verdict vs the median CPA (or CTR) of non-LOW-DATA ads: WIN <= 0.75x median CPA, CUT >= 1.5x, else OK (CTR mode: WIN >= 1.33x, CUT <= 0.67x). LOW DATA ads get verdict LOW DATA. Hook type tie-break: first matching of the list below. Group by format and by hook type (question, number/offer, first-person story, pain/"stop", curiosity, plain announcement): totals and the same ratios.
Flag LOW DATA when an ad has under 1,000 impressions or under 3 conversions; never call a LOW DATA ad the winner without saying so.

## 3. Output (in this order)
**Ranked table** (markdown): rank, ad, hook (short), hook type, format, spend, CTR, CVR, CPA, verdict (WIN / OK / CUT).
**Format and hook-type rollup**: 2 short tables.
**Why**: one line per ad, citing a number ("CTR 3.2% vs median 1.6%: the first-person hook earned the click; CVR held at 6%"). Separate click problems (low CTR: hook) from landing problems (good CTR, low CVR: offer or page).
**Pattern**: 2-3 bullets on what the winners share.
**Next three scripts**: each built on the winning pattern, one testing a new angle. For each: name, format, hook (first line, under 12 words), body beats (video: 0-3s / 3-10s / 10-20s / CTA; static or carousel: headline, frames, CTA), and "tests:" one line. Use only claims present in the input; put any number or promise not in the data in [brackets] for the user to fill.
**ASSUMED**: anything inferred.
End with the elapsed time.

## 4. Rules
- Never invent results, prices or discounts. Never give budget, bid or pause advice beyond the CUT verdict.
- Never touch an ad account; read only. Never share without an explicit yes.
- Follow-ups ("make #2 a carousel", "shorter hooks") rewrite only the scripts, keeping the table.
